status_summary: The HUD Secretary announced a HUD task force under the Department of Government Efficiency effort in mid-February 2025, described as made up of HUD employees reviewing spending; political-appointee composition and an ideology mandate are not stated. On 2025-02-20 the Secretary announced cancellation of about $4 million in diversity-related contracts. HUD terminated 78 Fair Housing Initiatives Program grants on 2025-02-27; a federal court in Massachusetts issued a temporary restraining order on 2025-03-26, dissolved it on 2025-04-14 citing a Supreme Court stay that pointed such claims to the Court of Federal Claims, and the plaintiffs voluntarily dismissed the case on 2025-12-22. HUD also withdrew fair housing guidance through a 2025-09-17 memo, formalized in notices published 2026-04-06 (eight documents) and 2026-07-17 (13 Office of General Counsel documents).

timeline.event: The HUD Secretary announced cancellation of about $4 million in diversity-related contracts after launching a DOGE task force.

HUD published the interim final rule Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Revisions (90 FR 11020, effective 2025-04-02), repealing the 2021 AFFH interim final rule, one of the prior-administration actions the text targets.
A federal district court in Massachusetts issued a 14-day temporary restraining order requiring HUD to reinstate terminated Fair Housing Initiatives Program grants for the plaintiffs.

The district court dissolved the 2025-03-26 temporary restraining order, citing the Supreme Court stay in Department of Education v. California and concluding the grant-termination claims likely belonged in the Court of Federal Claims.

title: Create a HUD task force to reverse Biden-era progressive-ideology actions
uncertainties: The task force is documented in a HUD press release of 2025-02-13 (HUD No. 25-030, the number taken from the URL), read on hud.gov on 2026-10-26: it was established under the President's government efficiency executive order, is composed of HUD employees, will review how HUD spends taxpayer dollars and reports to the Secretary; it is not described as limited to political appointees or as charged with reversing ideology-based actions, and it does not mention DEI. Its charter and named membership were not found. The stage therefore rests on operative reversals by other instruments; several of those reversals (AFFH, PAVE, climate initiatives, guidance withdrawals) are tracked as their own records (c15-01, c15-05, c15-06, c15-10), so this record overlaps them. The AFFH interim final rule event is copied from the verified sibling record c15-01. Both guidance withdrawal notices (2026-04-06 and 2026-07-17) were read in full on federalregister.gov in review; neither mentions a task force. A Federal Register API query of HUD documents since 2026-04-01, run in review on 2026-10-18, found no guidance withdrawal notice after 2026-07-17. The temporary restraining order date (2025-03-26) and the 2025-12-22 dismissal come from a docket summary on clearinghouse.net, and the 2025-04-14 dissolution is recounted in the First Circuit's 2025-11-18 judgment; the district court docket itself could not be opened. The 2025-09-17 memo was read as a copy hosted by a law-firm blog; searches for a hud.gov copy returned only association, law-firm and public-inspection copies. The 2025-09-17 memo and the 2026-04-06 notice cover largely the same documents.
